Enigma Multiplayer PR Review Diff

Generated 2026-02-09 03:17:04. Base: upstream/master (085e2bda) → Working tree (HEAD 394aa02a). Diff hash: 7a0c8e6232fd.
How to use: Grouped by path. Each file begins with a narrative (Description, Where used, What changed vs upstream) followed by a red/green diff. Per-hunk notes are intentionally not embedded here; long-lived explanations are kept as code comments instead.

Refactoring proposals (not applied)

Scope note: The multiplayer branch already includes substantial restructuring (transport facade, explicit session state, centralized config, UI split files) to keep review and maintenance tractable. The items below are intentionally deferred because they add tooling or cross-language coordination not required for the initial multiplayer PR.
4) In-process integration tests with a fake transport
  • What it is: A deterministic harness that instantiates a host and N clients in-process and drives the multiplayer session with a fake transport that can simulate packet loss/reordering/latency without real sockets.
  • Why it helps: Multiplayer bugs are often timing-sensitive. A fake transport would allow CI to cover join/start/restart/resync/peer-leave reliably and prevent regressions that are otherwise hard to reproduce.
  • Why it is deferred: It adds a non-trivial test framework surface (fake transport, scripted ticking, fixtures) that maintainers may want to evaluate after the core feature set lands.
5) Single source of truth for Internet lobby protocol schema
  • What it is: Share an explicit schema between the C++ client and tools/internet_lobby_server.py so request/response formats cannot drift silently (today: a custom binary UDP lobby protocol implemented in both C++ and Python).
  • Why it helps: Internet mode spans two languages and a separately deployed service. A shared schema reduces compatibility breakage and simplifies future API extensions (capability negotiation, versioned endpoints).
  • Why it is deferred: Schema tooling/codegen increases build and deployment complexity. The initial PR keeps the server implementation intentionally minimal and dependency-light.

@@ -0,0 +1,419 @@
1# Multiplayer (User Guide + Architecture)
2
3This document covers the full multiplayer feature set. It is split into:
4
5- **User Guide**: how to use LAN/Internet multiplayer.
6- **Architecture**: how it works internally and how we avoid desync.
7
8It is not a changelog.
9
10## User Guide
11
12### Opening multiplayer
13
14From the main menu, choose **Network Game** to open the multiplayer lobby.
15
16### In-game controls (multiplayer)
17
18- `ESC`: open the in-game menu (local) and pause the session (global)
19- `SHIFT+ESC`: abort the current level immediately
20
21In multiplayer, the in-game menu is still shown, but it is stepped from the main loop (non-blocking).
22That keeps the multiplayer network pump alive while a menu is open.
23
24While at least one player has the menu open, all instances show the global pause screen. Other players
25may press `ESC` to open their own menu as well. The session resumes once all menus are closed.
26
27### Internet server configuration (once)
28
29Open **Options -> Multiplayer** and set:
30
31- **Lobby/Relay Server**: hostname or IP of the shared server (default: `CHANGEME`)
32- Ports:
33 - Lobby (UDP, default 12347)
34 - UDP relay (UDP, default 12348)
35 - TCP relay (TCP, default 12349)
36- Connection strategies (toggles):
37 - Direct connect
38 - UDP relay
39 - TCP relay
40
41If multiple strategies are enabled, clients try them in this order:
42
43`Direct` -> `UDP relay` -> `TCP relay` (skipping disabled strategies).
44
45### LAN mode (local network)
46
47LAN mode uses UDP broadcast discovery.
48
491) Start Enigma on two (or more) machines in the same LAN (or multiple instances locally).
502) Open **Network Game** on all machines.
513) The other players should appear in the lobby.
524) Pick a **Level Pack**.
535) Use **Maps for N** to filter maps by intended player count.
546) The host starts a game by clicking a level icon.
55
56### Internet mode (room code)
57
58Internet mode uses a lobby server for room membership and "start" coordination, then
59uses direct connect or relays for the actual game session.
60
611) Ensure the server host + ports are configured (Options -> Multiplayer).
622) Switch the lobby to **Internet mode**.
633) Host enters a **Room code** and clicks **Create Room**.
644) Other players enter the same room code and click **Join Room**.
655) Once players joined, only the host selects a level (clients show "Waiting for host...").
666) Host starts a game by clicking a level icon.
67
68If UDP is blocked (guest WiFi, corporate networks, VPNs), enable **TCP relay** as fallback.
69
70### Debugging toggles
71
72Set environment variables before launching Enigma:
73
74- `ENIGMA_MP_DEBUG=1` enables verbose multiplayer logs.
75- `ENIGMA_MP_FORCE_RELAY=1` forces relay use (skips direct connect), useful for testing.
76- `ENIGMA_MP_DUMP_STATE=1` dumps a one-time deterministic actor digest when a sync mismatch is detected.
77- `ENIGMA_MP_TRACE_WORLDINIT=1` traces how `WorldInitLevel()` initializes actors (useful for tracking controller/ownership changes from Lua/compat).
78
79## Architecture
80
81### High-level model: deterministic lockstep
82
83Multiplayer is deterministic lockstep:
84
85- Each instance runs the full simulation locally.
86- Inputs are exchanged per fixed tick.
87- The host distributes inputs but does not stream full authoritative state.
88- Periodic sync snapshots detect drift and can correct some divergence.
89
90This keeps latency low while maintaining a consistent world state.
91
92### Lobby discovery and start
93
94LAN discovery:
95
96- Each peer periodically broadcasts `LobbyAnnounce` over UDP broadcast.
97- The host starts by broadcasting `LobbyStart`.
98
99Internet discovery (room codes):
100
101- Server: `tools/internet_lobby_server.py` (UDP, default 12347)
102- Room membership uses Create/Join/Leave/Poll requests.
103- Rooms are removed when the last member has timed out.
104
105`LobbyStart` carries session metadata:
106
107- `session_id`
108- `seed` (for deterministic RNG)
109- `pack_name` (fully qualifies the map across level packs; clients switch to this pack before loading)
110- `expected_players`
111- `host_port`
112- `host_id`
113- map filter settings (minimum intended player count)
114
115### "Other players connecting..." start barrier
116
117At level start, the host may need to wait for clients to connect and send `READY` before the
118session can begin. To avoid desync and avoid "flashing" the world for a single frame:
119
120- The host and clients enter a dedicated waiting screen (`cls_waiting_for_network_start`).
121- The level is only shown once `SessionState::Phase` allows start.
122- The game timer only starts ticking once all players are ready.
123
124### Session transport options
125
126All game-session payloads use a single message protocol (`src/multiplayer_protocol.hh`).
127How those payloads are transported depends on connectivity:
128
1291) **Direct**: client connects to host via ENet (`host_ip:host_port`).
1302) **UDP relay**: client connects to relay via ENet; relay forwards ENet packets between client and host.
1313) **TCP relay**: client connects to relay via raw TCP; relay forwards framed payloads between client and host.
132
133To keep session logic independent of the concrete transport, multiplayer uses a small transport facade:
134
135- `src/multiplayer_transport.hh` / `src/multiplayer_transport.cc` provides one `Poll()` + `Send()` API.
136- Session code consumes that facade and does not branch on "direct vs relay" at every call site.
137
138#### ENet versioning (vendored vs system)
139
140Enigma historically shipped a vendored ENet (`lib-src/enet`, libenet 1.0). Most modern distro builds
141(Ubuntu/Debian, Homebrew) use system ENet (ENet 1.3.x).
142
143ENet API signatures differ between these versions (e.g. `enet_host_create`, `enet_host_connect`,
144`enet_socket_create`), so multiplayer uses `src/enet_ver.hh` and small shims to compile against both.
145
146Important: the **UDP relay uses ENet itself**, so the relay must be built against an ENet version
147compatible with the clients. In practice, that means using ENet 1.3.x for deployed Internet relays.
148
149### Keeping simulations in sync
150
151#### Input lockstep and delay
152
153- Inputs are queued per tick for all players.
154- `input::CanAdvanceTick()` enforces that a tick only advances once all inputs are present.
155- A fixed input delay (`kInputDelay`) sends inputs slightly ahead to absorb jitter.
156
157#### Input epoch
158
159Each start/restart increments an `input_epoch`:
160
161- `NET_START`, `NET_INPUT`, `NET_SYNC` carry the epoch.
162- Packets from a previous epoch are ignored.
163
164This prevents late packets from a prior level/restart from corrupting the new simulation.
165
166#### Drift detection: RNG + checksums
167
168Periodic `NET_SYNC` snapshots include:
169
170- tick
171- RNG state
172- player reference positions (p0/p1)
173- checksums over relevant world/actor state
174
175Clients compare these snapshots to local state:
176
177- If only RNG diverged, RNG is corrected without a resync.
178- If reference positions drift beyond `kSyncPosEpsilon` or RNG diverges (non-RNG-only case), a
179 *soft resync* is attempted after a short consecutive mismatch streak.
180- If actor checksums diverge without any position/RNG/world mismatch, a soft resync can still be
181 attempted, but only after a longer mismatch streak (actor checksums can be sensitive).
182- If the world checksum diverges *without* any position/RNG/actor mismatch ("world-only mismatch"),
183 we currently treat this as not auto-recoverable and show a "World desync detected. Please restart."
184 toast after repeated detections. (This is where a future hard-resync could go.)
185
186In debug logs this is visible in the `mp desync... flags(pos=... rand=... actor=... world=...) action=...`
187line, where `action` is one of:
188
189- `rng-fix`: RNG-only mismatch, fixed by setting local RNG to the snapshot value
190- `soft-resync`: position/RNG mismatch likely recoverable by resyncing actor state
191- `actor-resync`: actor checksum mismatch only (position/RNG/world match), resync after longer streak
192- `diagnostic-only`: checksum mismatch observed, but no recovery action taken
193
194##### Reference actor probing (multi-ball + "stable sinks")
195
196The "reference positions" (`p0`/`p1`) are not always a literal "main ball". Instead, for each player we
197choose a deterministic *probe actor* via `sync_reference_actor(player, tick)`:
198
199- Prefer steerable actors controlled by that player.
200- Use a stable sort key (kind/owner/controllers/color/name/id), not position.
201- Cycle the chosen probe deterministically over time.
202
203The cycling is crucial for levels where a player controls multiple marbles (e.g. Per.Oxyd meditation
204pearls). If a single fixed probe happens to be in a "stable sink" (for example: stuck in a hole), its
205position can remain identical across peers even while other controlled marbles diverge. Cycling ensures
206each controlled marble is eventually sampled and can trigger recovery.
207
208##### Checksum surface (what is hashed)
209
210The goal of checksums is to detect "world divergence" even if it does not show up as an obvious
211position mismatch yet (for example: rotors, stateful stones, puzzle elements, etc.).
212
213`WorldChecksum()` (see `src/world.cc`) hashes:
214
215- Level dimensions (`w`, `h`).
216- The *kind* and selected *state* of objects in the floor, stone, and item layers (for each tile).
217- The list of actors: stable ids and quantized physics state (position/velocity).
218- The list of "other" objects: stable id and kind (and selected state where applicable).
219
220Notes:
221
222- Positions and velocities are quantized before hashing to avoid false positives from tiny float drift.
223- The checksum is intended to be deterministic across platforms as long as object state enumeration
224 stays stable. If you change what is hashed, you change the desync detection behavior.
225
226#### Resync ("soft resync")
227
228When divergence is detected:
229
230- Client requests a resync from the host.
231- Host responds with a compact actor-state snapshot.
232- Client applies it and continues.
233
234Resync snapshots include, per actor:
235
236- stable identifiers (`object_id`, `kind_id`, and `name_hash` where available)
237- metadata that affects control (`owner`, `controllers`, `color`)
238- physics state (`pos`, `vel`)
239
240Applying a resync is intentionally conservative:
241
242- Snapshots are applied "as-is" (no velocity projection). Projecting positions forward by the
243 observed tick delta tends to amplify divergence in high-acceleration physics (rubberbands,
244 collisions).
245- To avoid gameplay side-effects, resync teleports update physics state and the spatial index only.
246- Actors are matched primarily by `object_id`, but fall back to `name_hash` (and finally to a
247 best-effort match by kind/owner/position). This is important for levels where scripting can
248 create identical actors in a non-deterministic order across peers (e.g. meditation pearls).
249- After applying, rubberband constraints are re-evaluated to avoid persistent post-resync drift in
250 multi-ball levels.
251
252If resync fails repeatedly, the session reports a desync.
253
254### Global pause (multiplayer)
255
256Because the simulation is lockstep and each instance must keep pumping the network, pausing is
257implemented as a replicated state derived from menu-open state:
258
259- Clients notify the host when their ESC menu opens/closes (`NET_MENU`).
260- The host broadcasts the resulting pause/unpause decision to all peers (`NET_PAUSE`).
261- While paused, the simulation tick does not advance and no inputs are emitted, but the network is
262 still polled so unpause/leave/disconnect is handled promptly.
263- All instances show a pause screen (`cls_multiplayer_paused`) while any player has the menu open.
264
265### Extra players on low-player maps (non-optimized mode)
266
267If more players join than the map was authored for:
268
269- The first N players use authored start positions.
270- If the authored level provides fewer steerable actors (balls) than session players, additional
271 players are handled by *duplication + placement*:
272 - duplicate a "base" actor (usually the base player's main marble/ball)
273 - auto-place that duplicate on a safe, free floor tile near the base start position:
274 - prefer the closest safe, free floor tile with clear sight to the base start
275 - fall back to a random free tile if needed
276- If the authored level provides more steerable actors (balls) than session players (common for
277 Per.Oxyd "Meditation" levels), players are handled by *redistribution* instead:
278 - do not spawn new balls
279 - distribute the authored steerable actors as evenly as possible across the session players
280 (for 2 players and 4 balls: 2+2; for 3 players and 4 balls: 2+1+1)
281 - existing relationships between balls (e.g. rubberbands) remain exactly as authored; only
282 which player controls which ball changes
283
284The host broadcasts placements so all instances spawn identically.
285
286Notes:
287
288- Control assignment uses the explicit `controllers` bitmask on each actor. The legacy engine also
289 supports control-by-`color` for old levels that never set controllers. In multiplayer we rely on
290 controllers to be authoritative, so `Actor::controlled_by()` only falls back to `color` when
291 `controllers == 0`. This allows distributing multiple same-colored balls (e.g. all-white pearls)
292 across multiple players without changing their gameplay color.
293
294- Redistribution is performed both before and after `WorldInitLevel()`. Some compatibility
295 modes and Lua init code can overwrite `controllers` during initialization (notably meditation
296 pearls created via old API mappings). The post-init pass ensures the final runtime controller
297 masks match the intended distribution.
298
299### Restarts / next level
300
301Restarts are host-authoritative:
302
303- Host sends `NET_RESTART`.
304- Clients restart via network-specific entry points (avoids host-only guards).
305
306This ensures all instances restart in lockstep.
307
308## Key code locations
309
310The refactor splits multiplayer into small translation units with focused responsibilities:
311
312- Lobby:
313 - `src/multiplayer_lan_lobby.cc` (UDP broadcast lobby)
314 - `src/multiplayer_internet_lobby.cc` (room-code lobby client)
315 - `tools/internet_lobby_server.py` (room-code lobby server)
316- Session protocol:
317 - `src/multiplayer_protocol.hh` (binary session protocol and lobby packets)
318 - `src/multiplayer_relay_codec.cc` (relay framing header)
319- Session runtime/state machine:
320 - `src/multiplayer_internal.hh` (shared state structs and enums)
321 - `src/multiplayer_session_runtime.cc` (high-level session API used by `src/multiplayer.cc`)
322 - `src/multiplayer_session_transport.cc` (packet dispatch and transport sink)
323 - `src/multiplayer_session_start.cc` (join/start/restart transitions)
324 - `src/multiplayer_session_sync.cc` (sync/checksum/resync helpers)
325- Transport implementations:
326 - `src/multiplayer_transport.cc` (transport facade: poll + send/broadcast)
327 - `src/multiplayer_enet_socket.cc` (ENet API shims and setup)
328 - `src/multiplayer_tcp_socket.cc` (raw TCP relay socket)
329 - `tools/relay_server.cc` (UDP/ENet relay)
330 - `tools/tcp_relay_server.cc` (TCP relay)
331- UI:
332 - `src/gui/MultiplayerMenu.cc` + helpers in `src/gui/MultiplayerMenu_*.cc`
333 - `src/gui/OptionsMenu.cc` (Multiplayer options tab)
334
335## Deployment
336
337### Docker (single container)
338
339For Internet play, both services can be run in one container:
340
341- `tools/internet_lobby_server.py` (UDP lobby)
342- `tools/relay_server.cc` (UDP ENet relay)
343- `tools/tcp_relay_server.cc` (TCP relay fallback)
344
345The Docker image builds the UDP relay against distro ENet (`libenet-dev`) to match typical client
346builds that use system ENet.
347
348```sh
349docker build -t enigma-mp .
350docker run --rm \
351 -p 12347:12347/udp \
352 -p 12348:12348/udp \
353 -p 12349:12349/tcp \
354 enigma-mp
355```
356
357### Manual (no Docker)
358
359On Ubuntu/Debian you typically want:
360
361- `python3` for the lobby server
362- `libenet-dev` for the UDP relay
363
364Then run:
365
366- `python3 tools/internet_lobby_server.py --host 0.0.0.0 --port 12347`
367- `./enigma-relay --host 0.0.0.0 --port 12348`
368- `./enigma-tcp-relay --host 0.0.0.0 --port 12349`
369

3741/* -------------------- Value implementation -------------------- */
3842
43namespace {
44
45// Parse floating point numbers in a locale-independent way.
46//
47// XML level data and most config values are written with '.' as decimal separator.
48// Using locale-dependent atof() can truncate at '.' when LC_NUMERIC uses ',' which
49// would cause cross-platform desyncs in multiplayer (and wrong values in general).
50double parse_double_classic_locale(const char *s) {
51 if (!s)
52 return 0.0;
53
54 // Keep legacy "%<int>" escape behavior consistent with Value::operator int().
55 if (s[0] == '%')
56 return static_cast<double>(std::strtol(&(s[1]), NULL, 0));
57
58 std::string tmp(s);
59 // If the value looks like it uses ',' as decimal separator, normalize to '.'
60 // before parsing under the classic locale.
61 if (tmp.find('.') == std::string::npos && tmp.find(',') != std::string::npos) {
62 for (char &ch : tmp) {
63 if (ch == ',')
64 ch = '.';
65 }
66 }
67
68 std::istringstream iss(tmp);
69 iss.imbue(std::locale::classic());
70 double out = 0.0;
71 iss >> out;
72 return out;
73}
74
75} // namespace
76
3977 Value::Value() : type (NIL) {
4078 }

255293 case STRING:

257295 default:
258296 return 0.0;

289void Client::handle_events_waiting_for_network_start() {
290 SDL_Event e;

292 switch (e.type) {
293 case SDL_QUIT:
294 client::Msg_Command("abort");
295 app.bossKeyPressed = true;
296 break;
297 case SDL_WINDOWEVENT:
298 if (e.window.event == SDL_WINDOWEVENT_EXPOSED) {
299 draw_screen();
300 } else if (e.window.event == SDL_WINDOWEVENT_FOCUS_LOST) {
301 handle_focus_lost();
302 } else if (e.window.event == SDL_WINDOWEVENT_FOCUS_GAINED) {
303 handle_focus_gained();
304 }
305 break;
306 default:
307 // Ignore input while waiting: start is deferred and we don't want to
308 // queue a burst of inputs that will be applied all at once later.
309 break;
310 }
311 }

339 } else if (e.window.event == SDL_WINDOWEVENT_FOCUS_LOST) {
340 handle_focus_lost();
341 } else if (e.window.event == SDL_WINDOWEVENT_FOCUS_GAINED) {
342 handle_focus_gained();
343 }
344 break;
345 default:
346 break;
347 }
348 }

38void MultiplayerMenu::handle_level_activated() {
39 refresh_selection();
40 if (internet_mode) {
41 if (!internet_in_room) {
42 show_info(_("Create or join a room to start."));
43 return;
44 }
45 if (!internet_is_host) {
46 show_info(_("Waiting for host."));
47 return;
48 }
49 if (desired_players() < 2) {
50 show_info(_("Need at least two players to start."));
51 return;
52 }
53
54 // Ensure the start message fully qualifies the level across packs.
55 if (selected_pack_name.empty())
56 select_pack_for_level(selected_level_id);
57 multiplayer::protocol::LobbyStart start = multiplayer::BuildStartMessage(
58 selected_level_id, desired_players(), selected_pack_name, filter_min_players);
59 std::string error;
60 std::string server = mp_menu::multiplayer_server_host_from_options();
61 std::string room = current_room_code();
62 mp_menu::InternetServers servers = mp_menu::resolve_internet_servers(server);
63 if (!multiplayer::InternetStartRoom(mp_menu::resolved_lobby_server(server, servers),
64 room, start, error)) {
65 show_info(error.empty() ? _("Failed to start room.") : error);
66 return;
67 }
68 start_host_and_enter_game(start, false);
69 return;
70 }
71
72 if (!multiplayer::LoadMultiplayerConfig().enable_direct) {
73 show_info(_("Enable Direct Connect for LAN mode."));
74 return;
75 }
76 if (desired_players() < 2) {
77 show_info(_("Need at least two players to start."));
78 return;
79 }
80 if (!can_start()) {
81 show_info(_("Need matching players to start."));
82 return;
83 }
84 if (selected_pack_name.empty())
85 select_pack_for_level(selected_level_id);
86 multiplayer::protocol::LobbyStart start = multiplayer::BuildStartMessage(
87 selected_level_id, desired_players(), selected_pack_name, filter_min_players);
88 start_host_and_enter_game(start, true);
89}
90
91void MultiplayerMenu::handle_level_pack() {
92 if (internet_mode && internet_in_room && !internet_is_host) {
93 show_info(_("Waiting for host."));
94 return;
95 }
96 if (!selected_pack_name.empty())
97 lev::Index::setCurrentIndex(selected_pack_name);
98 LevelPackMenu menu(true);
99 menu.manage();
100 lev::Index *current = lev::Index::getCurrentIndex();
101 if (current) {
102 selected_pack_name = current->getName();
103 previous_index_name = selected_pack_name;
104 previous_index_pos = current->getCurrentPosition();
105 }
106 if (!lev::Index::setCurrentIndex(lobby_index->getName()))
107 return;
108 rebuild_index();
109 refresh_selection();
110 invalidate_all();
111}
112
113void MultiplayerMenu::handle_filter() {
114 if (internet_mode && internet_in_room && !internet_is_host) {
115 show_info(_("Waiting for host."));
116 return;
117 }
118 unsigned players = desired_players();
119 if (filter_min_players >= players)
120 filter_min_players = 1;
121 else
122 filter_min_players += 1;
123 update_filter_button();
124 rebuild_index();
125 refresh_selection();
126 invalidate_all();
127}
128
129void MultiplayerMenu::handle_mode_toggle() {
130 set_internet_mode(!internet_mode);
131 rebuild_index();
132 refresh_selection();
133 invalidate_all();
134}
135
136void MultiplayerMenu::handle_create_room() {
137 if (current_room_code().empty()) {
138 show_info(_("please choose room code"));
139 return;
140 }
141 unsigned players = desired_players();
142 std::string server = mp_menu::multiplayer_server_host_from_options();
143 std::string room_code = current_room_code();
144 mp_menu::InternetServers servers = mp_menu::resolve_internet_servers(server);
145 if (servers.lobby.empty()) {
146 show_info(_("Invalid server address."));
147 return;
148 }
149 multiplayer::SetRelayServer(servers.udp_relay);
150 multiplayer::SetTcpRelayServer(servers.tcp_relay);
151 if (selected_pack_name.empty())
152 select_pack_for_level(selected_level_id);
153 multiplayer::protocol::LobbyStart start = multiplayer::BuildStartMessage(
154 selected_level_id, players, selected_pack_name, filter_min_players);
155 std::string error;
156 if (!multiplayer::InternetCreateRoom(servers.lobby, room_code, start, error)) {
157 show_info(error.empty() ? _("Failed to create room.") : error);
158 return;
159 }
160 internet_room_code = room_code;
161 internet_start = start;
162 internet_start_valid = true;
163 internet_in_room = true;
164 internet_is_host = true;
165 internet_connecting = false;
166 internet_player_count = 1;
167 update_internet_layout();
168 show_info(_("Room created. Click a level to start."));
169}
170
171void MultiplayerMenu::handle_join_room() {
172 std::string server = mp_menu::multiplayer_server_host_from_options();
173 std::string room = current_room_code();
174 if (room.empty()) {
175 show_info(_("please choose room code"));
176 return;
177 }
178 mp_menu::InternetServers servers = mp_menu::resolve_internet_servers(server);
179 if (servers.lobby.empty()) {
180 show_info(_("Invalid server address."));
181 return;
182 }
183 multiplayer::SetRelayServer(servers.udp_relay);
184 multiplayer::SetTcpRelayServer(servers.tcp_relay);
185 multiplayer::protocol::LobbyStart start;
186 std::string host_ip;
187 std::string error;
188 unsigned player_count = 0;
189 if (!multiplayer::InternetJoinRoom(servers.lobby, room, start, host_ip, player_count, error)) {
190 show_info(error.empty() ? _("Failed to join room.") : error);
191 return;
192 }
193 internet_room_code = room;
194 internet_in_room = true;
195 internet_is_host = false;
196 internet_connecting = false;
197 internet_player_count = player_count > 0 ? player_count : 1;
198 update_internet_layout();
199 internet_poll_timer = 0.0;
200 show_info(_("Waiting for host."));
201}
202
203void MultiplayerMenu::handle_leave_room() {
204 leave_current_internet_room();
205 show_info(_("Left room."));
206}
207
208void MultiplayerMenu::on_action(gui::Widget *w) {
209 if (w == levelwidget) {
210 handle_level_activated();
211 return;
212 }
213 if (w == levelpack_button) {
214 handle_level_pack();
215 return;
216 }
217 if (w == filter_button) {
218 handle_filter();
219 return;
220 }
221 if (w == mode_button) {
222 handle_mode_toggle();
223 return;
224 }
225 if (w == create_room_button) {
226 handle_create_room();
227 return;
228 }
229 if (w == join_room_button) {
230 handle_join_room();
231 return;
232 }
233 if (w == leave_room_button) {
234 handle_leave_room();
235 return;
236 }
237 if (w == back_button)
238 Menu::quit();
239}

57lev::Index *find_pack_for_level_id(const std::string &level_id, lev::Index *lobby_index) {
58 std::vector<std::string> groups = lev::Index::getGroupNames();
59 for (const auto &group : groups) {
60 std::vector<lev::Index *> *indices = lev::Index::getGroup(group);
61 if (!indices)
62 continue;
63 for (auto *index : *indices) {
64 if (!index || index == lobby_index)
65 continue;
66 if (index->hasNormLevelPath(level_id))
67 return index;
68 }
69 }
70 return nullptr;
71}
72
73InternetServers resolve_internet_servers(const std::string &server) {
74 static_cast<void>(server);
75 multiplayer::MultiplayerConfig cfg = multiplayer::LoadMultiplayerConfig();
76 return multiplayer::ResolveInternetServers(cfg);
77}
78
79std::string multiplayer_server_host_from_options() {
80 multiplayer::MultiplayerConfig cfg = multiplayer::LoadMultiplayerConfig();
81 return cfg.server_host.empty() ? std::string("CHANGEME") : cfg.server_host;
82}
83
84bool proxy_player_info(lev::Proxy *proxy, unsigned &players, bool &optimized) {
85 if (!proxy)
86 return false;
87 try {
88 proxy->loadMetadata(true);
89 } catch (XLevelLoading &) {
90 return false;
91 }
92 bool network = proxy->hasNetworkMode();
93 bool single = proxy->hasSingleMode();
94 if (!network && !single)
95 return false;
96 optimized = network;
97 players = network ? proxy->getNetworkPlayers() : 1;
98 if (players < 1)
99 players = 1;
100 return true;
101}
102
103std::string no_level_message(unsigned min_players, unsigned desired_players) {
104 if (min_players == desired_players) {
105 return ecl::strf(_("No %u player levels are in this level pack"), desired_players);
106 }
107 return ecl::strf(_("No %u-%u player levels are in this level pack"), min_players,
108 desired_players);
109}
110
111std::string resolved_lobby_server(const std::string &server, const InternetServers &servers) {
112 return servers.lobby.empty() ? server : servers.lobby;
113}

49void MultiplayerMenu::rebuild_index() {
50 if (!lobby_index)
51 return;
52 std::string keep = selected_level_id;
53 lobby_index->clear();
54 unsigned desired_players_count = desired_players();
55 unsigned min_players = filter_min_players;
56 if (min_players < 1)
57 min_players = 1;
58 if (min_players > desired_players_count)
59 min_players = desired_players_count;
60
61 lev::Index *pack_index = nullptr;
62 if (!selected_pack_name.empty())
63 pack_index = lev::Index::findIndex(selected_pack_name);
64 if (!pack_index)
65 pack_index = lev::Index::getCurrentIndex();
66 if (!pack_index) {
67 info_label->set_text(mp_menu::no_level_message(min_players, desired_players_count));
68 info_ttl = -1.0;
69 lev::Index::setCurrentIndex(lobby_index->getName());
70 levelwidget->syncFromIndexMgr();
71 return;
72 }
73
74 std::vector<lev::Proxy *> proxies;
75 if (pack_index) {
76 proxies.reserve(static_cast<size_t>(pack_index->size()));
77 for (int i = 0; i < pack_index->size(); ++i) {
78 if (lev::Proxy *proxy = pack_index->getProxy(i))
79 proxies.push_back(proxy);
80 }
81 }
82
83 std::vector<lev::Proxy *> filtered;
84 filtered.reserve(proxies.size());
85 lev::RatingManager *ratings = lev::RatingManager::instance();
86 for (auto *proxy : proxies) {
87 unsigned players = 0;
88 bool optimized = false;
89 if (!mp_menu::proxy_player_info(proxy, players, optimized))
90 continue;
91 if (players > desired_players_count)
92 continue;
93 if (players < min_players)
94 continue;
95 filtered.push_back(proxy);
96 }
97
98 std::sort(filtered.begin(), filtered.end(),
99 [ratings](lev::Proxy *a, lev::Proxy *b) {
100 short da = ratings ? ratings->getDifficulty(a) : 0;
101 short db = ratings ? ratings->getDifficulty(b) : 0;
102 if (da != db)
103 return da < db;
104 std::string ta = a->getTitle();
105 std::string tb = b->getTitle();
106 if (ta != tb)
107 return ta < tb;
108 return a->getNormLevelPath() < b->getNormLevelPath();
109 });
110
111 for (auto *proxy : filtered)
112 lobby_index->appendProxy(proxy);
113
114 if (lobby_index->size() == 0)
115 selected_level_id.clear();
116
117 if (filtered.empty()) {
118 info_label->set_text(mp_menu::no_level_message(min_players, desired_players_count));
119 info_ttl = -1.0;
120 } else if (info_ttl < 0.0) {
121 info_label->set_text("");
122 info_ttl = 0.0;
123 }
124
125 lev::Index::setCurrentIndex(lobby_index->getName());
126 if (!keep.empty())
127 set_level_by_id(keep);
128 levelwidget->syncFromIndexMgr();
129}

203void MultiplayerMenu::update_internet_layout() {
204 int offscreen = -10000;
205 int x = internet_mode ? internet_form_x : offscreen;
206 int y = internet_mode ? internet_form_y : offscreen;
207 bool show_levels = internet_mode && internet_in_room && internet_is_host;
208 if (!internet_mode) {
209 room_label->move(offscreen, offscreen);
210 room_field->move(offscreen, offscreen);
211 players_label->move(offscreen, offscreen);
212 players_field->move(offscreen, offscreen);
213 internet_buttons->set_area(Rect(offscreen, offscreen,
214 internet_buttons->get_w(),
215 internet_buttons->get_h()));
216 internet_leave_buttons->set_area(Rect(offscreen, offscreen,
217 internet_leave_buttons->get_w(),
218 internet_leave_buttons->get_h()));
219 levelwidget->set_area(level_area);
220 waiting_label->move(offscreen, offscreen);
221 invalidate_all();
222 return;
223 }
224 if (show_levels) {
225 levelwidget->set_area(level_area);
226 waiting_label->move(offscreen, offscreen);
227 } else {
228 levelwidget->set_area(Rect(offscreen, offscreen, level_area.w, level_area.h));
229 if (!internet_in_room)
230 waiting_label->set_text(_("Create or join a room."));
231 else if (internet_connecting)
232 waiting_label->set_text(_("Connecting..."));
233 else
234 waiting_label->set_text(_("Waiting for host..."));
235 waiting_label->move(level_area.x, level_area.y + level_area.h / 2 - 10);
236 }
237 room_label->move(x, y);
238 room_field->move(x, y + room_label->get_h());
239 players_label->move(offscreen, offscreen);
240 players_field->move(offscreen, offscreen);
241 int buttons_w = internet_buttons->get_w();
242 int buttons_h = internet_buttons->get_h();
243 int leave_w = internet_leave_buttons->get_w();
244 int leave_h = internet_leave_buttons->get_h();
245 internet_buttons->set_area(Rect(internet_in_room ? offscreen : internet_buttons_x,
246 internet_in_room ? offscreen : internet_buttons_y,
247 buttons_w, buttons_h));
248 internet_leave_buttons->set_area(Rect(internet_in_room ? internet_buttons_x : offscreen,
249 internet_in_room ? internet_buttons_y : offscreen,
250 leave_w, leave_h));
251 bool lock_fields = internet_in_room;
252 room_field->set_locked(lock_fields);
253 create_room_button->set_text(N_("Create Room"));
254 invalidate_all();
255}

257unsigned MultiplayerMenu::desired_players() const {
258 if (!internet_mode)
259 return multiplayer::LobbySize() == 0 ? 1 : multiplayer::LobbySize();
260 if (internet_in_room && internet_player_count > 0)
261 return internet_player_count;
262 unsigned players = 0;
263 if (parse_players_field(players))
264 return players;
265 return 2;

268bool MultiplayerMenu::parse_players_field(unsigned &players) const {
269 if (!players_field)
270 return false;
271 std::string text = players_field->getText();
272 if (text.empty())
273 return false;
274 char *end = nullptr;
275 long value = std::strtol(text.c_str(), &end, 10);
276 if (!end || *end != '\0')
277 return false;
278 if (value < 1)
279 value = 1;
280 if (value > static_cast<long>(input::kMaxPlayers))
281 value = input::kMaxPlayers;
282 players = static_cast<unsigned>(value);
283 return true;
284}

286void MultiplayerMenu::update_players() {
287 std::vector<multiplayer::LobbyPeer> peers;
288 if (internet_mode) {
289 unsigned count = internet_player_count > 0 ? internet_player_count : 1;
290 multiplayer::LobbyPeer self;
291 self.name = "Player";
292 self.is_self = true;
293 peers.push_back(self);
294 for (unsigned i = 1; i < count; ++i) {
295 multiplayer::LobbyPeer peer;
296 peer.name = "Player";
297 peer.is_self = false;
298 peers.push_back(peer);
299 }
300 } else {
301 peers = multiplayer::LobbyPeers();
302 if (peers.empty()) {
303 multiplayer::LobbyPeer self;
304 self.name = "Player";
305 self.is_self = true;
306 peers.push_back(self);
307 }
308 std::sort(peers.begin(), peers.end(),
309 [](const multiplayer::LobbyPeer &a, const multiplayer::LobbyPeer &b) {
310 if (a.is_self != b.is_self)
311 return a.is_self;
312 return a.name < b.name;
313 });
314 }
315 for (size_t i = 0; i < player_labels.size(); ++i) {
316 if (i < peers.size()) {
317 std::string label = peers[i].name;
318 if (peers[i].is_self) {
319 label += " (you)";
320 }
321 player_labels[i]->set_text(label);
322 } else {
323 player_labels[i]->set_text("");
324 }
325 }
326}

328bool MultiplayerMenu::can_start() const {
329 if (selected_level_id.empty())
330 return false;
331 if (desired_players() < 2)
332 return false;
333 if (required_players() > input::kMaxPlayers)
334 return false;
335 if (internet_mode)
336 return desired_players() >= required_players();
337 if (!multiplayer::LoadMultiplayerConfig().enable_direct)
338 return false;
339 return multiplayer::LobbySize() >= required_players();
340}

350 return 1;
351 return players;

55void MultiplayerMenu::leave_current_internet_room() {
56 // Leaving should cancel any in-progress join attempt (it can keep retrying for a
57 // while via timeouts even though the UI is already back in the lobby).
58 multiplayer::CancelClientJoin();
59 internet_join_in_progress = false;
60 lan_join_in_progress = false;
61
62 std::string server = mp_menu::multiplayer_server_host_from_options();
63 mp_menu::InternetServers servers = mp_menu::resolve_internet_servers(server);
64 std::string error;
65 std::string room = !internet_room_code.empty() ? internet_room_code : current_room_code();
66 if (!multiplayer::InternetLeaveRoom(mp_menu::resolved_lobby_server(server, servers),
67 room, error)) {
68 // Best-effort: even if the leave packet did not get an ACK, we still leave locally.
69 // The server will eventually expire stale rooms, and the user can re-join if needed.
70 if (!error.empty())
71 show_info(error);
72 }
73 clear_internet_room_state();
74 update_internet_layout();
75}

77void MultiplayerMenu::show_transport_info(int transport_kind) {
78 switch (static_cast<multiplayer::TransportKind>(transport_kind)) {
79 case multiplayer::TransportKind::TCP_RELAY:
80 show_info(_("Using TCP relay (higher latency)."));
81 break;
82 case multiplayer::TransportKind::UDP_RELAY:
83 show_info(_("Using UDP relay."));
84 break;
85 case multiplayer::TransportKind::DIRECT:
86 show_info(_("Using direct connection."));
87 break;
88 default:
89 break;
90 }
91}

109 // This mirrors what the host did when selecting the pack via LevelPackMenu.

123bool MultiplayerMenu::start_host_and_enter_game(const multiplayer::protocol::LobbyStart &start,

131 // where clients attempt to connect before the host socket is bound.
132 multiplayer::LobbyBroadcastStart(start);

134 enter_game_from_lobby();

162 tick_lan_mode(dtime);
163 else
164 tick_internet_mode(dtime);
165
166 update_players();
167 refresh_selection();
168
169 if (info_ttl > 0.0) {
170 info_ttl -= dtime;
171 if (info_ttl <= 0.0)
172 info_label->set_text("");
173 }
174}
175
176void MultiplayerMenu::tick_lan_mode(double dtime) {
177 multiplayer::LobbyTick(dtime);
178 unsigned lobby_size = multiplayer::LobbySize();
179 if (lobby_size != last_lobby_size) {
180 last_lobby_size = lobby_size;
181 rebuild_index();
182 refresh_selection();
183 invalidate_all();
184 }
185
186 if (lan_join_in_progress) {
187 multiplayer::ClientJoinStatus st = poll_client_join_and_maybe_enter_game();
188 if (st == multiplayer::ClientJoinStatus::FAILED) {
189 show_info(_("Failed to join host. LAN play requires direct UDP connectivity."));
190 lan_last_join_failed = true;
191 lan_join_in_progress = false;
192 } else if (st == multiplayer::ClientJoinStatus::JOINED) {
193 lan_join_in_progress = false;
194 }
195 }
196
197 multiplayer::protocol::LobbyStart start;
198 std::vector<std::string> host_ips;
199 if (!multiplayer::LobbyPollStart(start, host_ips))
200 return;
201
202 if (start.session_id != lan_last_join_session_id) {
203 lan_last_join_session_id = start.session_id;
204 lan_last_join_failed = false;
205 multiplayer::CancelClientJoin();
206 lan_join_in_progress = false;
207 }
208 if (lan_last_join_failed)
209 return;
210
211 apply_start_selection(start);
212 lan_join_start = start;
213 lan_join_host_ip = host_ips.empty() ? std::string() : host_ips[0];
214 if (!begin_client_join(start, host_ips)) {
215 show_info(_("Failed to join host. LAN play requires direct UDP connectivity."));
216 lan_last_join_failed = true;
217 lan_join_in_progress = false;
218 } else {
219 lan_join_in_progress = true;
220 }
221 refresh_selection();
222}
223
224void MultiplayerMenu::tick_internet_mode(double dtime) {
225 if (internet_join_in_progress) {
226 multiplayer::ClientJoinStatus st = poll_client_join_and_maybe_enter_game();
227 if (st == multiplayer::ClientJoinStatus::FAILED) {
228 show_info(_("Failed to join host."));
229 internet_last_join_failed = true;
230 internet_join_in_progress = false;
231 set_internet_connecting(false);
232 } else if (st == multiplayer::ClientJoinStatus::JOINED) {
233 internet_join_in_progress = false;
234 set_internet_connecting(false);
235 }
236 }
237
238 if (!internet_in_room) {
239 multiplayer::CancelClientJoin();
240 internet_join_in_progress = false;
241 return;
242 }
243
244 internet_poll_timer += dtime;
245 if (internet_poll_timer < 0.2)
246 return;
247 internet_poll_timer = 0.0;
248
249 std::string server = mp_menu::multiplayer_server_host_from_options();
250 std::string room = room_field ? room_field->getText() : "";
251 mp_menu::InternetServers servers = mp_menu::resolve_internet_servers(server);
252 multiplayer::protocol::LobbyStart start;
253 std::string host_ip;
254 std::string error;
255 bool started = false;
256 unsigned player_count = 0;
257 if (!multiplayer::InternetPollRoom(mp_menu::resolved_lobby_server(server, servers), room,
258 start, host_ip, started, player_count, error)) {
259 if (!error.empty() && error != "waiting")
260 show_info(error);
261 return;
262 }
263
264 if (player_count > 0 && player_count != internet_player_count) {
265 internet_player_count = player_count;
266 update_players();
267 invalidate_all();
268 }
269 if (!started) {
270 internet_last_join_session_id = 0;
271 internet_last_join_failed = false;
272 multiplayer::CancelClientJoin();
273 internet_join_in_progress = false;
274 set_internet_connecting(false);
275 return;
276 }
277 if (internet_is_host)
278 return;
279
280 if (start.session_id != internet_last_join_session_id) {
281 internet_last_join_session_id = start.session_id;
282 internet_last_join_failed = false;
283 multiplayer::CancelClientJoin();
284 internet_join_in_progress = false;
285 set_internet_connecting(false);
286 }
287 if (internet_last_join_failed)
288 return;
289
290 apply_start_selection(start);
291 if (!internet_join_in_progress) {
292 set_internet_connecting(true);
293 internet_join_start = start;
294 internet_join_host_ip = host_ip;
295 std::vector<std::string> host_ips;
296 if (!host_ip.empty())
297 host_ips.push_back(host_ip);
298 if (!begin_client_join(start, host_ips)) {
299 show_info(_("Failed to join host."));
300 internet_last_join_failed = true;
301 internet_join_in_progress = false;
302 set_internet_connecting(false);
303 } else {
304 internet_join_in_progress = true;
305 }
306 }
307 refresh_selection();
308}
309

311} // namespace enigma

A src/input.cc

Description
  • Input abstraction implementation.
Where it is used
  • Used by gameplay loop.
What changed vs upstream/master
  • Implements injected-input plumbing required for lockstep multiplayer.
diff --git a/src/input.cc b/src/input.cc
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..776218ec
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/input.cc
@@ -0,0 +1,149 @@
1#include "input.hh"
2
3#include <bitset>
4#include <map>
5
6namespace enigma {
7namespace input {
8
9namespace {
10
11struct TickInputs {
12 std::array<PlayerInput, kMaxPlayers> inputs;
13 std::bitset<kMaxPlayers> present;
14};
15
16bool g_networked = false;
17unsigned g_expected_players = 1;
18uint32_t g_current_tick = 0;
19std::array<PlayerInput, kMaxPlayers> g_local_pending;
20std::map<uint32_t, TickInputs> g_queue;
21
22PlayerInput empty_input() {
23 return PlayerInput();
24}
25
26bool valid_player(unsigned player) {
27 return player < kMaxPlayers;
28}
29
30} // namespace
31
32void Reset() {
33 g_current_tick = 0;
34 g_queue.clear();
35 g_networked = false;
36 g_expected_players = 1;
37 for (auto &pending : g_local_pending)
38 pending = PlayerInput();
39}
40
41void SetNetworked(bool enabled) {
42 g_networked = enabled;
43}
44
45bool IsNetworked() {
46 return g_networked;
47}
48
49void SetExpectedPlayers(unsigned count) {
50 g_expected_players = count;
51}
52
53unsigned ExpectedPlayers() {
54 return g_expected_players;
55}
56
57uint32_t CurrentTick() {
58 return g_current_tick;
59}
60
61void SubmitMouseForce(unsigned player, const ecl::V2 &force) {
62 if (!valid_player(player))
63 return;
64 g_local_pending[player].mouse_force += force;
65}
66
67void SubmitRotateInventory(unsigned player, int dir) {
68 if (!valid_player(player))
69 return;
70 g_local_pending[player].rotate_steps += dir;
71}
72
73void SubmitActivateItem(unsigned player) {
74 if (!valid_player(player))
75 return;
76 g_local_pending[player].activate_count += 1;
77}
78
79PlayerInput DrainLocalPending(unsigned player) {
80 if (!valid_player(player))
81 return empty_input();
82 PlayerInput pending = g_local_pending[player];
83 g_local_pending[player] = PlayerInput();
84 return pending;
85}
86
87void EnqueueInput(uint32_t tick, unsigned player, const PlayerInput &input) {
88 if (!valid_player(player))
89 return;
90 TickInputs &slot = g_queue[tick];
91 slot.inputs[player].merge(input);
92 slot.present.set(player);
93}
94
95bool HasInput(uint32_t tick, unsigned player) {
96 if (!valid_player(player))
97 return false;
98 auto it = g_queue.find(tick);
99 if (it == g_queue.end())
100 return false;
101 return it->second.present.test(player);
102}
103
104bool PeekInput(uint32_t tick, unsigned player, PlayerInput &out) {
105 if (!valid_player(player))
106 return false;
107 auto it = g_queue.find(tick);
108 if (it == g_queue.end())
109 return false;
110 if (!it->second.present.test(player))
111 return false;
112 out = it->second.inputs[player];
113 return true;
114}
115
116bool CanAdvanceTick() {
117 if (!g_networked)
118 return true;
119 if (g_expected_players == 0)
120 return false;
121 for (unsigned player = 0; player < g_expected_players; ++player) {
122 if (!HasInput(g_current_tick, player))
123 return false;
124 }
125 return true;
126}
127
128PlayerInput ConsumeInput(uint32_t tick, unsigned player) {
129 if (!valid_player(player))
130 return empty_input();
131 if (!g_networked)
132 return DrainLocalPending(player);
133 auto it = g_queue.find(tick);
134 if (it == g_queue.end() || !it->second.present.test(player))
135 return empty_input();
136 PlayerInput input = it->second.inputs[player];
137 it->second.inputs[player] = PlayerInput();
138 it->second.present.reset(player);
139 if (it->second.present.none())
140 g_queue.erase(it);
141 return input;
142}
143
144void AdvanceTick() {
145 ++g_current_tick;
146}
147
148} // namespace input
149} // namespace enigma

@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
1#ifndef INPUT_HH_INCLUDED
2#define INPUT_HH_INCLUDED
3
4#include "ecl_math.hh"
5
6#include <array>

A src/multiplayer_ball_assignment.hh

Description
  • Helpers for mapping steerable actors (balls/marbles) to session players.
  • Encapsulates deterministic distribution: add extra balls when players > balls, redistribute balls when balls > players (meditation levels).
Where it is used

What changed vs upstream/master

  • Introduces deterministic round-robin assignment so all instances derive the same per-player ball ownership.

22/* -------------------- Multiplayer ball assignment -------------------- */
23/*
24 * Helpers for deterministic ball-to-player assignment.
25 *
26 * Used by the "more balls than players" path (meditation-like levels) to split
27 * authored actors across controllers while keeping the level's rubberbands and
28 * other connections intact.
29 */
30
31#include <cstddef>
32#include <vector>
33
34namespace enigma {
35namespace multiplayer {
36namespace internal {
37
38// Returns a per-ball assignment to players, distributing balls as evenly as
39// possible in a deterministic round-robin order.
40//
41// The caller decides whether redistribution is appropriate (e.g. only when the
42// authored level provides enough balls for all players in a color-group).
43inline std::vector<unsigned> distribute_balls_round_robin(size_t ball_count,
44 const std::vector<unsigned> &players) {
45 std::vector<unsigned> out;
46 out.reserve(ball_count);
47 if (players.empty()) {
48 for (size_t i = 0; i < ball_count; ++i)
49 out.push_back(0);
50 return out;
51 }
52 for (size_t i = 0; i < ball_count; ++i)
53 out.push_back(players[i % players.size()]);
54 return out;
55}
56
57} // namespace internal
58} // namespace multiplayer
59} // namespace enigma
60
61#endif // MULTIPLAYER_BALL_ASSIGNMENT_HH_INCLUDED

33namespace enigma {
34namespace multiplayer {
35
36namespace {
37
38bool force_relay_enabled() {
39 const char *env = std::getenv("ENIGMA_MP_FORCE_RELAY");
40 return env && *env;
41}
42
43std::uint16_t clamp_port(int value, std::uint16_t fallback) {
44 if (value > 0 && value <= 65535)
45 return static_cast<std::uint16_t>(value);
46 return fallback;
47}
48
49std::string sanitize_host_only(const std::string &raw) {
50 std::string host = raw;
51 if (host.empty())
52 host = "CHANGEME";
53 // Backwards-compat: if the saved config still contains host:port, strip the port.
54 std::string::size_type port_sep = host.rfind(':');
55 if (port_sep != std::string::npos)
56 host = host.substr(0, port_sep);
57 if (host == "localhost" || host == "::1")
58 host = "127.0.0.1";
59 if (host.empty())
60 host = "CHANGEME";
61 return host;
62}
63
64} // namespace
65
66MultiplayerConfig LoadMultiplayerConfig() {
67 MultiplayerConfig cfg;
68 cfg.server_host = sanitize_host_only(options::GetString("MultiplayerLobbyServer"));
69 cfg.lobby_port = clamp_port(options::GetInt("MultiplayerInternetLobbyPort"), 12347);
70 cfg.udp_relay_port = clamp_port(options::GetInt("MultiplayerInternetUdpRelayPort"), 12348);
71 cfg.tcp_relay_port = clamp_port(options::GetInt("MultiplayerInternetTcpRelayPort"), 12349);
72 cfg.enable_direct = options::GetBool("MultiplayerEnableDirect");
73 cfg.enable_udp_relay = options::GetBool("MultiplayerEnableUdpRelay");
74 cfg.enable_tcp_relay = options::GetBool("MultiplayerEnableTcpRelay");
75 cfg.force_relay = force_relay_enabled();
76 return cfg;
77}
78
79InternetServers ResolveInternetServers(const MultiplayerConfig &cfg) {
80 InternetServers out;
81 if (cfg.server_host.empty() || cfg.server_host == "CHANGEME")
82 return out;
83 out.lobby = cfg.server_host + ":" + std::to_string(cfg.lobby_port);
84 out.udp_relay = cfg.server_host + ":" + std::to_string(cfg.udp_relay_port);
85 out.tcp_relay = cfg.server_host + ":" + std::to_string(cfg.tcp_relay_port);
86 return out;
87}

81void debug_log(const char *fmt, ...) {
82 if (!debug_enabled())
83 return;
84
85#ifdef WIN32
86 // GUI-subsystem binaries often have no attached console, so stderr can be
87 // discarded. When ENIGMA_MP_DEBUG is enabled, also write to a temp log file
88 // so Windows builds remain debuggable.
89 static FILE *log_file = nullptr;
90 static bool log_file_init = false;
91 if (!log_file_init) {
92 log_file_init = true;
93 const char *tmp = std::getenv("TEMP");
94 if (!tmp || !*tmp)
95 tmp = std::getenv("TMP");
96 if (!tmp || !*tmp)
97 tmp = ".";
98 char path[1024] = {0};
99 std::snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s/enigma-mp-%d.log", tmp, _getpid());
100 log_file = std::fopen(path, "a");
101 }
102#endif
103
104 // Prefix every log line with stable session context so host/client logs
105 // can be correlated even when per-level tick counters reset.
106 static uint64_t seq = 0;
107 seq += 1;
108 const unsigned sid = static_cast<unsigned>(g_session.session_id);
109 const unsigned rid = static_cast<unsigned>(g_session.restart_id);
110 const unsigned epoch = static_cast<unsigned>(g_session.input_epoch);
111 const unsigned lp = static_cast<unsigned>(g_session.local_player);
112 const int is_host = g_session.host ? 1 : 0;
113 const char *via = transport_kind_name(g_session.active_transport);
114
115 va_list args;
116 va_start(args, fmt);
117 std::fprintf(stderr, "mp[%llu sid=%u rid=%u epoch=%u host=%d p=%u via=%s] ",
118 static_cast<unsigned long long>(seq), sid, rid, epoch, is_host, lp, via);
119 std::vfprintf(stderr, fmt, args);
120 std::fprintf(stderr, "\n");
121 std::fflush(stderr);
122
123#ifdef WIN32
124 if (log_file) {
125 va_list args2;
126 va_copy(args2, args);
127 std::fprintf(log_file, "mp[%llu sid=%u rid=%u epoch=%u host=%d p=%u via=%s] ",
128 static_cast<unsigned long long>(seq), sid, rid, epoch, is_host, lp, via);
129 std::vfprintf(log_file, fmt, args2);
130 std::fprintf(log_file, "\n");
131 std::fflush(log_file);
132 va_end(args2);
133 }
134#endif
135
136 va_end(args);
137}

139std::string address_to_ip_string(const ENetAddress &addr) {
140 // Always prefer a numeric IPv4 address here. LAN multiplayer uses this
141 // address for direct connects; reverse DNS / hostnames can fail to resolve
142 // (notably on Windows).
143 in_addr ia;
144 ia.s_addr = addr.host; // ENet stores host in network byte order.
145#ifdef WIN32
146 const char *s = inet_ntoa(ia);
147 return s ? std::string(s) : std::string();
148#else
149 char buf[INET_ADDRSTRLEN] = {0};
150 if (!inet_ntop(AF_INET, &ia, buf, sizeof(buf)))
151 return std::string();
152 return std::string(buf);
153#endif
154}

32/* -------------------- Multiplayer ENet socket -------------------- */
33/*
34 * ENet API compatibility wrappers.
35 *
36 * System ENet and vendored ENet differ in some low-level APIs across versions.
37 * Multiplayer uses these wrappers to compile and behave consistently.
38 */
39
40namespace enigma {
41namespace multiplayer {
42namespace internal {
43
44ENetSocket enet_socket_create_compat(ENetSocketType type) {
45#ifdef ENET_VER_EQ_GT_13
46 return enet_socket_create(type);
47#else
48 return enet_socket_create(type, nullptr);
49#endif
50}
51
52void tune_enet_socket(ENetSocket socket, bool broadcast) {
53 if (socket == ENET_SOCKET_NULL)
54 return;
55
56 int opt = 1;
57#ifdef WIN32
58 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, reinterpret_cast<const char *>(&opt), sizeof(opt));
59 if (broadcast)
60 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_BROADCAST, reinterpret_cast<const char *>(&opt), sizeof(opt));
61 u_long mode = 1;
62 ioctlsocket(socket, FIONBIO, &mode);
63#else
64 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, &opt, sizeof(opt));
65 if (broadcast)
66 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_BROADCAST, &opt, sizeof(opt));
67
68 // Force non-blocking behavior across ENet variants. We never want UI/game
69 // loops to block on a recvfrom()/sendto().
70 int flags = fcntl(socket, F_GETFL, 0);
71 if (flags != -1)
72 (void)fcntl(socket, F_SETFL, flags | O_NONBLOCK);
73#endif
74
75 // Increase buffers a bit to reduce packet loss under load.
76 int buf_sz = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB
77#ifdef WIN32
78 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVBUF, reinterpret_cast<const char *>(&buf_sz), sizeof(buf_sz));
79 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_SNDBUF, reinterpret_cast<const char *>(&buf_sz), sizeof(buf_sz));
80#else
81 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVBUF, &buf_sz, sizeof(buf_sz));
82 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_SNDBUF, &buf_sz, sizeof(buf_sz));
83#endif
84}
85
86bool bind_lobby_socket(ENetSocket socket, Uint16 port) {
87 int opt = 1;
88#ifdef WIN32
89 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, reinterpret_cast<const char *>(&opt), sizeof(opt));
90#ifdef SO_REUSEPORT
91 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEPORT, reinterpret_cast<const char *>(&opt), sizeof(opt));
92#endif
93 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_BROADCAST, reinterpret_cast<const char *>(&opt), sizeof(opt));
94 u_long mode = 1;
95 ioctlsocket(socket, FIONBIO, &mode);
96#else
97 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, &opt, sizeof(opt));
98#ifdef SO_REUSEPORT
99 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEPORT, &opt, sizeof(opt));
100#endif
101 setsockopt(socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_BROADCAST, &opt, sizeof(opt));
102
103 // Make the lobby socket non-blocking. Some ENet builds do not set this by
104 // default, and a blocking recvfrom() would stall the UI loop.
105 int flags = fcntl(socket, F_GETFL, 0);
106 if (flags != -1) {
107 (void)fcntl(socket, F_SETFL, flags | O_NONBLOCK);
108 }
109#endif
110
111 sockaddr_in sin;
112 ::memset(&sin, 0, sizeof(sin));
113 sin.sin_family = AF_INET;
114 sin.sin_port = ENET_HOST_TO_NET_16(port);
115 sin.sin_addr.s_addr = ENET_HOST_ANY;
116 bool ok = bind(socket, reinterpret_cast<sockaddr *>(&sin), sizeof(sin)) == 0;
117 if (ok) {
118 // Make sure socket behaves consistently across ENet builds.
119 tune_enet_socket(socket, true);
120 }
121 return ok;
122}
123
124} // namespace internal
125} // namespace multiplayer
126} // namespace enigma

38/* -------------------- Multiplayer extra players -------------------- */
39/*
40 * Extra-player support for "non-optimized" levels.
41 *
42 * When a level was authored for N players but the lobby has M > N players, the
43 * session either spawns additional actors (M > N) or redistributes authored
44 * steerable actors (N > M) depending on the level's ball layout.

54 if (!proxy)
55 return players;

57 proxy->loadMetadata(true);
58 } catch (XLevelLoading &) {
59 return players;

61 if (proxy->hasNetworkMode())
62 return proxy->getNetworkPlayers();
63 if (proxy->hasSingleMode())
64 return 1;

76bool controller_single_bit_index(int controllers, unsigned &out_index) {
77 if (controllers <= 0)
78 return false;
79 unsigned mask = static_cast<unsigned>(controllers);
80 if ((mask & (mask - 1)) != 0)
81 return false;
82 unsigned idx = 0;
83 while ((mask & 1u) == 0u) {
84 mask >>= 1u;
85 idx += 1u;
86 }
87 out_index = idx;
88 return true;
89}

110bool is_passable_for_sight(const GridPos &pos) {
111 if (!IsInsideLevel(pos))
112 return false;
113 Floor *floor = GetFloor(pos);
114 if (!floor)
115 return false;
116 const std::string kind = floor->getKind();
117 if (kind == "fl_abyss" || kind == "fl_water" || kind == "fl_space" ||
118 kind == "fl_space_force") {
119 return false;
120 }
121 if (GetStone(pos) != nullptr)

123 if (GetItem(pos) != nullptr)
124 return false;
125 return true;

135 if (kind == "fl_abyss" || kind == "fl_water" || kind == "fl_space" ||
136 kind == "fl_space_force") {
137 return false;
138 }
139 if (GetStone(pos) != nullptr)
140 return false;
141 if (GetItem(pos) != nullptr)
142 return false;
143 std::vector<Actor *> actors;
144 GetActorsInsideField(pos, actors);
145 if (!actors.empty())

162bool has_clear_sight(const GridPos &from, const GridPos &to) {
163 int x0 = from.x;
164 int y0 = from.y;
165 int x1 = to.x;
166 int y1 = to.y;
167 int dx = std::abs(x1 - x0);
168 int dy = std::abs(y1 - y0);
169 int sx = (x0 < x1) ? 1 : -1;
170 int sy = (y0 < y1) ? 1 : -1;
171 int err = dx - dy;
172
173 int x = x0;
174 int y = y0;
175 while (true) {
176 if (!(x == x0 && y == y0) && !(x == x1 && y == y1)) {
177 if (!is_passable_for_sight(GridPos(x, y)))
178 return false;
179 }
180 if (x == x1 && y == y1)
181 break;
182 int e2 = 2 * err;
183 if (e2 > -dy) {
184 err -= dy;
185 x += sx;
186 }
187 if (e2 < dx) {
188 err += dx;
189 y += sy;
190 }
191 }
192 return true;
193}
194
195bool find_clear_floor_near_base(const GridPos &base_pos, GridPos &out_pos) {
196 int tiles_x = 0;
197 int tiles_y = 0;
198 int origin_x = 0;
199 int origin_y = 0;
200 if (!screen_bounds_for_base(base_pos, origin_x, origin_y, tiles_x, tiles_y))
201 return false;
202 int best_dist = std::numeric_limits<int>::max();
203 bool found = false;
204 for (int pass = 0; pass < 2; ++pass) {
205 for (int y = origin_y; y < origin_y + tiles_y; ++y) {
206 for (int x = origin_x; x < origin_x + tiles_x; ++x) {
207 GridPos pos(x, y);
208 if (pass == 0) {
209 if (!is_safe_floor(pos))
210 continue;
211 } else {
212 if (!is_free_floor(pos))
213 continue;
214 }
215 if (!has_clear_sight(base_pos, pos))
216 continue;
217 int dx = x - base_pos.x;
218 int dy = y - base_pos.y;
219 int dist = dx * dx + dy * dy;
220 if (dist < best_dist) {
221 best_dist = dist;
222 out_pos = pos;
223 found = true;
224 }
225 }
226 }
227 if (found)
228 return true;
229 }
230 return false;
231}
232
233bool find_random_free_tile(const GridPos &base_pos, GridPos &out_pos) {
234 int tiles_x = 0;
235 int tiles_y = 0;
236 int origin_x = 0;
237 int origin_y = 0;
238 std::vector<GridPos> free_tiles;
239 if (screen_bounds_for_base(base_pos, origin_x, origin_y, tiles_x, tiles_y)) {
240 for (int y = origin_y; y < origin_y + tiles_y; ++y) {
241 for (int x = origin_x; x < origin_x + tiles_x; ++x) {
242 GridPos pos(x, y);
243 if (is_free_floor(pos))
244 free_tiles.push_back(pos);
245 }
246 }
247 if (!free_tiles.empty()) {
248 int idx = enigma::IntegerRand(0, static_cast<int>(free_tiles.size() - 1), true);
249 out_pos = free_tiles[static_cast<size_t>(idx)];
250 return true;
251 }
252 }
253 free_tiles.clear();
254 int width = Width();
255 int height = Height();
256 for (int y = 0; y < height; ++y) {
257 for (int x = 0; x < width; ++x) {
258 GridPos pos(x, y);
259 if (is_free_floor(pos))
260 free_tiles.push_back(pos);
261 }
262 }
263 if (free_tiles.empty())
264 return false;
265 int idx = enigma::IntegerRand(0, static_cast<int>(free_tiles.size() - 1), true);
266 out_pos = free_tiles[static_cast<size_t>(idx)];
267 return true;
268}

270template <class Sender>
271void for_each_existing_placement(Sender send) {
272 if (!g_session.host)
273 return;
274 if (g_session.expected_players <= g_session.level_players || g_session.level_players == 0)
275 return;
276 if (g_session.placement_received.size() < g_session.expected_players)
277 return;
278 for (unsigned player = g_session.level_players; player < g_session.expected_players; ++player) {
279 // Only players that actually required placement during this level should get
280 // placement packets. Players that don't require placement are marked
281 // placement_received=true so the host can start immediately, but that does
282 // not mean we have a meaningful placement to broadcast.
283 if (!placement_required_for_player(player))
284 continue;
285 if (!g_session.placement_received[player])
286 continue;
287 Actor *actor = player::GetMainActor(player);
288 if (!actor)
289 continue;
290 GridPos pos = actor->get_gridpos();
291 protocol::PlacementPacket msg;
292 msg.restart_id = g_session.restart_id;
293 msg.player = static_cast<Uint8>(player);
294 msg.x = static_cast<Uint16>(pos.x);
295 msg.y = static_cast<Uint16>(pos.y);
296 send(msg);
297 }
298}

300void send_placement_to_peer(ENetPeer *peer, const protocol::PlacementPacket &msg) {
301 if (!peer)
302 return;
303 ecl::Buffer buf;
304 protocol::encode_place(buf, msg);
305 ENetPacket *packet = enet_packet_create(buf.data(), buf.size(), ENET_PACKET_FLAG_RELIABLE);
306 enet_peer_send(peer, 0, packet);
307}

311bool is_valid_placement(const GridPos &pos, unsigned player) {
312 if (!is_free_floor(pos))

316 unsigned base_player = player % g_session.level_players;
317 Actor *base_actor = player::GetMainActor(base_player);
318 if (!base_actor)
319 return true;
320 int tiles_x = 0;
321 int tiles_y = 0;
322 int origin_x = 0;
323 int origin_y = 0;
324 GridPos base_pos(base_actor->get_startpos());
325 if (!screen_bounds_for_base(base_pos, origin_x, origin_y, tiles_x, tiles_y))
326 return true;
327 if (pos.x < origin_x || pos.x >= origin_x + tiles_x)
328 return false;
329 if (pos.y < origin_y || pos.y >= origin_y + tiles_y)
330 return false;
331 return true;
332}

369 ecl::Buffer buf;
370 protocol::encode_place(buf, msg);
371 g_transport.HostSendTcpRelay(client_id, buf);
372 });
373}
374
375void send_placement_to_host(const GridPos &pos) {
376 if (!g_session.active)
377 return;
378 protocol::PlacementPacket msg;
379 msg.restart_id = g_session.restart_id;
380 msg.player = static_cast<Uint8>(g_session.local_player);
381 msg.x = static_cast<Uint16>(pos.x);
382 msg.y = static_cast<Uint16>(pos.y);
383 if (g_session.host) {
384 if (placement_required_for_player(msg.player) && is_valid_placement(pos, msg.player)) {
385 apply_placement(msg.player, pos);
386 if (g_session.placement_received.size() > msg.player)
387 g_session.placement_received[msg.player] = true;
388 broadcast_placement(msg);
389 }
390 return;
391 }
392 ecl::Buffer buf;
393 protocol::encode_place(buf, msg);
394 g_transport.ClientSend(buf);
395}
396
397void auto_place_extra_players() {
398 if (!g_session.host)
399 return;
400 if (g_session.level_players == 0)
401 return;
402 for (unsigned player = g_session.level_players; player < g_session.expected_players; ++player) {
403 if (!placement_required_for_player(player))
404 continue;
405 unsigned base_index = player % g_session.level_players;
406 Actor *base_actor = player::GetMainActor(base_index);
407 if (!base_actor)
408 continue;
409 GridPos base_pos(base_actor->get_startpos());
410 GridPos pos;
411 bool found = find_clear_floor_near_base(base_pos, pos);
412 if (!found)
413 found = find_random_free_tile(base_pos, pos);
414 if (!found)
415 continue;
416 protocol::PlacementPacket msg;
417 msg.restart_id = g_session.restart_id;
418 msg.player = static_cast<Uint8>(player);
419 msg.x = static_cast<Uint16>(pos.x);
420 msg.y = static_cast<Uint16>(pos.y);
421 apply_placement(player, pos);
422 if (g_session.placement_received.size() > player)
423 g_session.placement_received[player] = true;
424 broadcast_placement(msg);
425 }
426}

428void add_extra_actors(unsigned level_players, unsigned expected_players) {
429 g_session.needs_placement.clear();
430 if (expected_players > 0)
431 g_session.needs_placement.assign(expected_players, false);
432 if (level_players == 0 || expected_players <= level_players)
433 return;
434 std::vector<Actor *> actors;
435 GetActors(actors);
436 if (debug_enabled())
437 debug_log("mp extra actors: level_players=%u expected=%u actors=%zu", level_players,
438 expected_players, actors.size());
439
440 rebalance_authored_multi_ball_levels(level_players, expected_players);
441
442 // Track which session players already control a steerable actor after
443 // redistribution, to avoid spawning unnecessary duplicates.
444 std::vector<bool> has_actor(expected_players, false);
445 for (auto *actor : actors) {
446 if (!actor || !actor->isSteerable())
447 continue;
448 int controllers = actor->get_controllers();
449 unsigned owner = 0;
450 if (!controller_single_bit_index(controllers, owner))
451 continue;
452 if (owner >= expected_players)
453 continue;
454 has_actor[owner] = true;
455 }
456
457 std::vector<Actor *> base(level_players, nullptr);
458 std::vector<Actor *> fallback(level_players, nullptr);
459 Actor *any_actor = nullptr;
460
461 for (auto *actor : actors) {
462 if (!any_actor && actor->isSteerable())
463 any_actor = actor;
464 unsigned owner = 0;
465 bool has_owner = false;
466 if (Value owner_val = actor->getAttr("owner")) {
467 int owner_int = owner_val;
468 if (owner_int >= 0 && owner_int < static_cast<int>(level_players)) {
469 owner = static_cast<unsigned>(owner_int);
470 has_owner = true;
471 }
472 }
473 if (!has_owner) {
474 unsigned ctrl_owner = 0;
475 if (controller_single_bit_index(actor->get_controllers(), ctrl_owner) &&
476 ctrl_owner < level_players) {
477 owner = ctrl_owner;
478 has_owner = true;
479 }
480 }
481 if (!has_owner)
482 continue;
483 if (!fallback[owner])
484 fallback[owner] = actor;
485 if (!base[owner]) {
486 int controllers = actor->get_controllers();
487 if ((controllers & (1 << owner)) != 0 && actor->isSteerable())
488 base[owner] = actor;
489 }
490 }
491
492 for (unsigned i = 0; i < level_players; ++i) {
493 if (!base[i])
494 base[i] = fallback[i];
495 }
496
497 if (!any_actor) {
498 for (auto *candidate : base) {
499 if (candidate) {
500 any_actor = candidate;
501 break;
502 }
503 }
504 }
505
506 for (unsigned player = level_players; player < expected_players; ++player) {
507 if (player < has_actor.size() && has_actor[player])
508 continue;
509 unsigned base_index = (level_players > 0) ? (player % level_players) : 0;
510 Actor *base_actor = base_index < base.size() ? base[base_index] : nullptr;
511 if (!base_actor)
512 base_actor = any_actor;
513 if (!base_actor)
514 continue;
515 Actor *extra = MakeActor(base_actor->getKind().c_str());
516 if (!extra)
517 continue;
518 extra->setAttr("owner", Value(static_cast<int>(player)));
519 extra->setAttr("controllers", Value(static_cast<int>(1 << player)));
520 extra->setAttr("essential", Value(0));
521 Value color = base_actor->getAttr("color");
522 if (color.getType() != Value::NIL)
523 extra->setAttr("color", color);
524 ecl::V2 pos = base_actor->get_pos();
525 AddActor(pos[0], pos[1], extra);
526 if (player < g_session.needs_placement.size())
527 g_session.needs_placement[player] = true;
528 }
529
530 if (debug_enabled()) {
531 unsigned have = 0;
532 for (bool v : has_actor)
533 if (v)
534 have += 1;
535 unsigned need_place = 0;
536 for (bool v : g_session.needs_placement)
537 if (v)
538 need_place += 1;
539 debug_log("mp extra actors: assigned=%u spawned=%u needs_placement=%u", have,
540 (expected_players > have) ? (expected_players - have) : 0, need_place);
541 }
542}
543
544void rebalance_authored_multi_ball_levels(unsigned level_players, unsigned expected_players) {
545 if (level_players == 0 || expected_players <= level_players)
546 return;
547 std::vector<Actor *> actors;
548 GetActors(actors);
549
550 // Redistribution pass: some authored levels (e.g. meditation) give one player
551 // multiple steerable actors. If there are enough such actors, distribute them
552 // evenly across all session players that share the same color group
553 // (player % level_players), instead of spawning new duplicates.
554 std::vector<std::vector<Actor *>> candidates(level_players);
555 for (auto *actor : actors) {
556 if (!actor || !actor->isSteerable())
557 continue;
558
559 // For singleplayer-authored levels, treat all steerable, player-controlled
560 // actors as belonging to the single base group. Some compatibility modes
561 // and conversions (notably Per.Oxyd meditation pearls) may leave "owner"
562 // unset or set to a non-zero value, but the level intent is still
563 // "controlled by the (single) current player".
564 if (level_players == 1) {
565 if (actor->get_controllers() == 0) {
566 Value owner_val = actor->getAttr("owner");
567 Value color_val = actor->getAttr("color");
568 if (!owner_val && !color_val)
569 continue;
570 }
571 candidates[0].push_back(actor);
572 continue;
573 }
574
575 bool found_base = false;
576 unsigned base = 0;
577
578 // Prefer the authored owner if present. This covers many singleplayer
579 // multi-ball levels where the engine default sets controllers=CTRL_YINYANG
580 // (e.g. pearls), but the level intent is still "owned by player 0".
581 if (Value owner_val = actor->getAttr("owner")) {
582 int owner_int = owner_val;
583 if (owner_int >= 0 && owner_int < static_cast<int>(level_players)) {
584 base = static_cast<unsigned>(owner_int);
585 found_base = true;
586 }
587 }
588
589 // Fallback: single-controller actors that don't declare an owner.
590 if (!found_base) {
591 unsigned ctrl_base = 0;
592 if (controller_single_bit_index(actor->get_controllers(), ctrl_base) &&
593 ctrl_base < level_players) {
594 base = ctrl_base;
595 found_base = true;
596 }
597 }
598
599 // Legacy singleplayer actors sometimes leave owner unset but still default to
600 // controllers=CTRL_YINYANG (e.g. pearls created via old API mappings). In
601 // singleplayer metadata those are still effectively "owned by player 0".
602 if (!found_base && level_players == 1) {
603 if ((actor->get_controllers() & 1) != 0) {
604 base = 0;
605 found_base = true;
606 }
607 }
608
609 if (!found_base)
610 continue;
611 candidates[base].push_back(actor);
612 }
613
614 for (unsigned base = 0; base < level_players; ++base) {
615 // Ensure redistribution is deterministic across platforms/builds.
616 // Actor insertion order can differ subtly depending on loader/compat paths,
617 // so sort by a stable key before assigning controllers.
618 std::sort(candidates[base].begin(), candidates[base].end(),
619 [](const Actor *a, const Actor *b) {
620 if (a == b)
621 return false;
622 const ecl::V2 &pa = a->get_pos();
623 const ecl::V2 &pb = b->get_pos();
624 auto qa0 = static_cast<int64_t>(std::llround(pa[0] * 1000.0));
625 auto qa1 = static_cast<int64_t>(std::llround(pa[1] * 1000.0));
626 auto qb0 = static_cast<int64_t>(std::llround(pb[0] * 1000.0));
627 auto qb1 = static_cast<int64_t>(std::llround(pb[1] * 1000.0));
628 if (qa1 != qb1)
629 return qa1 < qb1;
630 if (qa0 != qb0)
631 return qa0 < qb0;
632 const ecl::V2 &va = a->get_vel();
633 const ecl::V2 &vb = b->get_vel();
634 auto qva0 = static_cast<int64_t>(std::llround(va[0] * 1000.0));
635 auto qva1 = static_cast<int64_t>(std::llround(va[1] * 1000.0));
636 auto qvb0 = static_cast<int64_t>(std::llround(vb[0] * 1000.0));
637 auto qvb1 = static_cast<int64_t>(std::llround(vb[1] * 1000.0));
638 if (qva1 != qvb1)
639 return qva1 < qvb1;
640 if (qva0 != qvb0)
641 return qva0 < qvb0;
642 int kind_cmp = a->getKind().compare(b->getKind());
643 if (kind_cmp != 0)
644 return kind_cmp < 0;
645 int ca = a->get_controllers();
646 int cb = b->get_controllers();
647 if (ca != cb)
648 return ca < cb;
649 Value oa = a->getAttr("owner");
650 Value ob = b->getAttr("owner");
651 int oai = oa ? static_cast<int>(oa) : -1;
652 int obi = ob ? static_cast<int>(ob) : -1;
653 if (oai != obi)
654 return oai < obi;
655 Value cola = a->getAttr("color");
656 Value colb = b->getAttr("color");
657 int cai = cola ? static_cast<int>(cola) : -1;
658 int cbi = colb ? static_cast<int>(colb) : -1;
659 if (cai != cbi)
660 return cai < cbi;
661 // If everything matches, the order does not matter: the actors are
662 // indistinguishable at our digest precision, and redistribution by
663 // position/velocity already yields the same per-player multiset.
664 return false;
665 });
666
667 std::vector<unsigned> group;
668 for (unsigned p = base; p < expected_players; p += level_players)
669 group.push_back(p);
670 if (group.size() <= 1)
671 continue;
672 if (candidates[base].size() < group.size())
673 continue; // Not enough authored balls; keep legacy duplication behavior.
674 if (debug_enabled())
675 debug_log("mp rebalance: base=%u candidates=%zu group=%zu", base, candidates[base].size(),
676 group.size());
677 std::vector<unsigned> assignment =
678 distribute_balls_round_robin(candidates[base].size(), group);
679 for (size_t i = 0; i < candidates[base].size(); ++i) {
680 Actor *a = candidates[base][i];
681 unsigned target = assignment[i];
682 a->setAttr("owner", Value(static_cast<int>(target)));
683 a->setAttr("controllers", Value(static_cast<int>(1 << target)));
684 }
685 }
686}

67constexpr double kResyncCooldown = 1.0;
68// If a resync request is in-flight for too long (packet loss, transport stall),
69// clear the in-flight flag so we can retry. Without this, a single lost resync
70// response can permanently disable recovery.
71constexpr double kResyncInflightTimeout = 2.5;
72// When aborting a session, keep the transport alive briefly so reliable abort
73// packets have a chance to reach peers (avoids prolonged desync spam on clients
74// if the host shuts down immediately).

77// a disconnect. This catches cases where a host exits too quickly for a
78// reliable abort to arrive.
79constexpr double kClientNoPayloadDisconnectTimeout = 2.0;
80// Require at least N consecutive mismatch observations before triggering a resync
81// request. This reduces "jumpy mode" when a single late/out-of-order sync sample
82// briefly disagrees but the world would converge again naturally.
83constexpr unsigned kDesyncStreakForResync = 2;
84// Actor checksum mismatches can be caused by platform drift. Only trigger a
85// resync from actor checksums when the mismatch persists for multiple sync
86// intervals.

88constexpr unsigned kResyncMaxAttempts = 3;
89constexpr size_t kChecksumHistory = 512;

91// not bit-identical across platforms, especially in physics-heavy levels (e.g.
92// rubberbands/meditation pearls). Keep this loose enough to avoid constant
93// resync churn, while still catching meaningful divergence.
